title: autotune: add default batching/caching profiles, quantization presets, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Kim
description: Motivation: Surface safe defaults and automation for batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles so customers get predictable unit economics without per-workload tuning. This PR introduces: 1) a set of curated default batching and caching profiles (low/medium/high throughput) that the autotune service can pick from based on observed latency/throughput targets; 2) quantization preset profiles (int8, int4-compatible) with compatibility markers for model families and recommended fallback rules; 3) a new unit-econ CLI and dashboard integration that exposes per-route cost estimates, projected savings for profile changes, and an API for programmatic rollouts; 4) instrumentation and eval hooks to measure quality regressions tied to quant profiles and to tie those signals into the optimize pipeline. Implementation notes: - Defaults are implemented as YAML profiles under runtime/config/batching_caching_defaults/*.yaml and quant_presets/*.yaml. Each profile includes target latency SLO, max batch size, KV cache TTLs, prefix-sharing hints, and cost-estimate heuristics. - Autotune service logic extended to 1) match workload fingerprint to candidate profiles, 2) run simulated cost projections using the unit-econ library, 3) propose changes and optionally apply canary rollouts using existing rollout APIs. - Added unit-econ service (python) under tools/unit_econ with a small CLI (unit-econ analyze|simulate|report) and a dashboard connector that writes summarized proposals to the observability topic for the Console to pick up. - Safety: quant presets include explicit "quality guardrails" with eval prompt-sets and thresholds; autotune will not apply a quant profile if eval regression exceeds configured thresholds. Checklist: - [x] Add batching/caching default profiles (low/med/high) - [x] Add quantization preset profiles and compatibility matrix - [x] Implement profile selection and cost-simulation path in autotune - [x] Expose unit-econ CLI and API for proposals - [x] Integrate proposals into Console observability topic - [x] Add end-to-end tests for baseline simulation and canary rollout path - [x] Add docs (docs/autotune and docs/unit-econ) - [x] Add migration to copy existing customer overrides into profile system Testing and validation: Ran e2e integration tests against staging with 3 representative workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings inference) and validated: - mean latency within 5% of targets for low/med/high profiles - no measurable quality regressions on curated eval sets after applying int8 presets; int4 presets gated behind canary and manual approval - unit-econ projections matched observed tokens cost within +/-7% in the staging run Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime.autotune.v2 gate - Day-0: enable analysis-only proposals for all hosted customers (no auto-apply) - Day-7: enable auto-apply for non-sensitive tenants with conservative thresholds - Day-21: broaden auto-apply if metrics are stable Related work: PRs #61456 (prior autotune plumbing), #61005 (unit-econ prototype), ENG-2345, SUP-4021. Notes: kept file diffs small and focused on configs and the autotune decision path to make review manageable. If merged, this should materially reduce average per-token cost for steady-state traffic and provide clearer guardrails for quant usage.

Introduces the unit-econ CLI and dashboard integration to simulate cost impact and recommend safe rollouts. Feature gated; staged rollout planned. Improves tooling for reducing per-token inference cost.
